requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`.

**Scope of the explicit-checkpoint backends.** The only backend that takes explicit checkpoints is Bedrock. `RigProvider::connect` sets `caches` only for Bedrock models that `bedrock_caches` accepts. Ollama and OpenAI always get `caches = false`.

**Bedrock obligations**
- **Support condition.** `providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` asserts `bedrock_caches` is true for Claude (plain id and inference-profile ARN) and Nova. It asserts false for Llama and for the fixture model. The CLI test also checks that a non-caching fixture model gets no `cachePoint` at all.
- **System-prompt checkpoint.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` checks that, in every cached request body, `system` has two entries. The first starts with the prompt text and the second is exactly `{"cachePoint":{"type":"default"}}`.
- **Last-message checkpoint.** The same test checks that the last element of the last message's content is the checkpoint.
- **Exactly two checkpoints.** The test counts `cachePoint` occurrences in each body and requires two.
- **"Every request".** The test covers both requests of the conversation. The second follows a reasoning turn and has three messages. A unit test in `providers.rs` also checks that a reasoning-turn history still gets the cache option.
- **No change to content.** `without_cache_points(cached)` must equal the body sent to the non-caching model, for each request. The unit test also compares the serialized request, which differs only in the cache option.

**OpenAI obligations**, in `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]`:
- `instructions` is non-empty and equal across the two requests.
- `tools` is equal across the two requests, and each request has 12 tools.
- The second request's `input` begins with the first request's `input` unchanged. It then appends the `function_call` and `function_call_output` for `call_id` "read", in that order. This covers replaying prior content in original order.
- `assert_no_checkpoints` runs on every request body. This covers the rule against inserting checkpoint blocks.

No obligation is missing a test, and no unacknowledged gap remains.

text: :::{req} cache_checkpoints
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
test-adequacy requirement, structural requirement, example, citation review, site
review. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
